title: One unplaceable-reference rule replaces six reference lints
summary: This change collapses six separate reference lints (bare-reference, reference-without-label, reference-without-link, chat-local-reference, undefined-name, undefined-name-at-start) into a single `unplaceable-reference` rule backed by a new 2.4k-line candidate engine in `crates/osf/src/lints/writing/reference.rs`. The engine finds numbers, phrases, times and names in a paragraph and asks whether the paragraph itself places them (a link, a bracketed description, a named repository, a file path, an absolute date, a known name, a definer sentence). It also introduces an `Evidence` axis: findings backed only by statistical evidence (a guessed name, a quoted term, a developer tool) resolve to Warning/Advise in every context, so a guess can never refuse a reply at the stop hook. The old rules still run beside the new one until they are retired, which is why the pre-commit test now expects two errors.

lanes.label: Text sources
lanes.subtitle: where a document enters the lint
lanes.summary: The surfaces that hand text to the writing lint: a chat reply at the stop hook, a commit message, a document on disk, and a skill file.

lanes.label: Lint core
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf-lint-core
lanes.summary: Shared machinery: text segmentation, the rule runner, and the class/group/context/evidence matrix that decides a finding's level and remediation.

lanes.label: Writing rules
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing
lanes.summary: The rule set itself. The new candidate engine and the placement check live here, beside the older reference rules they are replacing.

lanes.label: Verdict
lanes.subtitle: level, remediation, exit code
lanes.summary: Where a finding becomes a decision: a warning that advises, an error that asks for a rewrite, or a refusal that blocks the reply.

nodes.label: Stop hook
nodes.subtitle: hook stop reads the last assistant message
nodes.summary: Reads the session event from stdin, lints the last assistant message in transcript context, and exits 2 to refuse the reply when an error-level finding survives. A new test pins that a reply whose only finding is a weak-evidence name is not refused.

nodes.label: Commit-message check
nodes.subtitle: lint writing --context commit
nodes.summary: Lints a commit message file in commit context, where relative times and bare references are errors rather than transcript-only advice.

nodes.label: Document text
nodes.subtitle: markdown on disk
nodes.summary: A document read from disk, linted in document context. This is the context the new fixture corpus and the precision/recall measure exercise.

nodes.label: Skill file
nodes.subtitle: skill context
nodes.summary: A skill file linted in skill context, resolved through the same matrix as every other context.

nodes.label: Text segmentation
nodes.subtitle: segment::parse, TextUnit, reduce_inline
nodes.summary: Splits text into sentences and paragraphs and marks headings and list items. The new engine re-parses each paragraph and re-applies the unit's own heading and list-item flags so a re-parsed sentence does not lose them.

nodes.label: resolve() matrix
nodes.subtitle: class x group x context x exception x evidence
nodes.summary: Decides a finding's level and remediation. It now takes the finding's own Evidence and short-circuits: statistical evidence always resolves to Warning/Advise, in every context, class, group and exception, so a guess can never block a reply.

nodes.label: Rule runner
nodes.subtitle: run_rules, FnRule, Finding
nodes.summary: Runs each rule function over the parsed document and collects findings. The new rule is registered here as one more entry.

nodes.label: Known names
nodes.subtitle: built-in list plus project file
nodes.summary: The built-in name list and any project known-names file. New entries cover frameworks and model tiers (React, Vite, Tauri, RFC, Sonnet, Opus, Haiku), and a new is_generic_word accessor lets the number exclusion tell a real name from a generic label word such as Phase.

nodes.label: Candidate engine
nodes.subtitle: reference::candidates
nodes.summary: The new heart of the change. Finds number, phrase, time and name candidates in a paragraph, masks quoted and backticked spans so their content is never matched, and keeps only the longest candidate per kind when two overlap.

nodes.label: Number candidates
nodes.subtitle: #12, issue 31, mechanism (b), version 7
nodes.summary: Finds hash numbers, word-and-number labels and word-and-bracket letters, then excludes versions, ranges, years, clock times, percent quantities, counts of plural nouns, measures, coordinates and known names followed by a number.

nodes.label: Phrase candidates
nodes.subtitle: as discussed, the previous, above
nodes.summary: Finds configured chat-local phrases and the fixed phrase 'the previous', and tells a reference 'above' from the preposition by what follows it: a clause close, a determiner, or a postposed noun-and-verb shape.

nodes.label: Time candidates
nodes.subtitle: on Monday, the eighteenth, yesterday
nodes.summary: Finds bare ordinal days, weekdays and relative day words. Relative words are skipped entirely in transcript context, since a reply is read at the moment it is sent.

nodes.label: Name candidates
nodes.subtitle: DuckDB, "the done wave", moon
nodes.summary: Finds capitalised runs with real evidence (an inner capital, a digit, a domain suffix, or a repeated multi-word run) and lowercase double-quoted terms. In document context it also finds developer tool names, bare or backticked, unless the known-names list already covers them.

nodes.label: Placement check
nodes.subtitle: is_placed, per kind
nodes.summary: Asks whether the paragraph itself places each candidate: a link, a bracketed or colon description, a named repository, a file path or file name, a list item for a bracketed letter, an absolute date for a time, a known name or definer sentence for a name. A phrase is never placed.

nodes.label: unplaceable-reference
nodes.subtitle: one rule, four kinds
nodes.summary: The single rule that replaces the six retired ids. It reports one finding per unplaced candidate, at its first use for a repeated name, with a message that names what to add. Weak-evidence findings carry Evidence::Statistical.

nodes.label: Legacy reference rules
nodes.subtitle: bare-reference, chat-local-reference, undefined-name
nodes.summary: The six rules the new one replaces. They still run beside it until they are retired, which is why the pre-commit test now expects two errors for one message and why the writing tests filter the new rule out.

nodes.label: Rule metadata
nodes.subtitle: RULE_META, RuleMeta::resolve
nodes.summary: The doc text and class/group/exception for every rule. A new entry documents unplaceable-reference, and RuleMeta::resolve now forwards the finding's evidence into the shared matrix.

nodes.label: Finding
nodes.subtitle: level, remediation, evidence, excerpt
nodes.summary: A single lint result. It now carries an Evidence value that travels with it from the rule through the resolve matrix to the level and remediation it ends up with.

nodes.label: Refusal
nodes.subtitle: exit code 2 at the stop hook
nodes.summary: The stop hook refuses a reply when an error-level finding survives. Because statistical evidence always resolves to Warning/Advise, a guessed name can no longer reach this node on its own.

nodes.label: Unplaceable fixtures
nodes.subtitle: 98 labelled markdown cases
nodes.summary: A new fixture directory where each file carries an osf-unplaceable header naming its label, kind, target and reason. The corpus is the ground truth the precision/recall measure scores against.

nodes.label: Precision/recall measure
nodes.subtitle: unplaceable_measure.rs
nodes.summary: Runs the lint over every fixture, scores true and false positives and negatives per kind, and requires 100% precision and recall with no stray findings. The model kind is reported on its own row and excluded from the totals.

nodes.label: End-to-end checkpoints
nodes.subtitle: stop hook, commit check, prompt hook
nodes.summary: Drives the compiled binary: a bare fix number refuses the stop, a quoted mention does not, a relative time passes in a reply but fails the commit check, and the prompt reminder never names a deleted rule id.

edges.label: last assistant message
edges.summary: The stop hook hands the reply text to the writing lint in transcript context.

edges.label: candidates(unit, cfg, known, context, run counts)
edges.summary: The new rule calls the candidate engine once per paragraph, then asks the placement check about each candidate. This is the connection the change is really about.

edges.label: is this a real name?
edges.summary: The engine consults the known-names list to exclude a number after a real name and to skip a tool the project already knows, using the new is_generic_word accessor to keep generic label words out.

edges.label: is_placed(candidate)
edges.summary: Every candidate the engine finds is handed to the placement check, which decides whether the paragraph itself resolves it.

edges.label: unplaced candidate
edges.summary: An unplaced candidate becomes a finding carrying its excerpt, a message naming what to add, and an Evidence value.

edges.label: old findings
edges.summary: The six retired rules still emit their own findings beside the new one, which is why one message can now produce two errors.

edges.label: class, group, context, exception, evidence
edges.summary: The finding's evidence now travels into the resolve matrix, where statistical evidence short-circuits to Warning/Advise.

edges.label: error level only
edges.summary: Only an error-level finding can reach the refusal. Statistical evidence never resolves to error, so a guessed name cannot refuse a reply.

edges.label: 98 labelled cases
edges.summary: Each fixture's header names its label, kind, target and reason; the measure parses those headers and scores the lint against them.

edges.label: lint_writing over each fixture
edges.summary: The measure calls the lint directly over every fixture and requires 100% precision and recall with no stray findings.

edges.label: hook stop with stdin
edges.summary: The end-to-end tests spawn the compiled binary and write a session event to its stdin, proving the rule runs at the real stop hook.

flows.title: A chat reply through the stop hook
flows.summary: What happens to one assistant reply when the stop hook lints it: the candidate engine finds a bare fix number, the placement check finds nothing in the paragraph that resolves it, and the finding reaches the refusal.

messages.label: last assistant message
messages.note: The hook reads the session event from stdin and hands the reply text to the writing lint in transcript context.

messages.label: Candidate { kind: Number, text: "fix 5" }
messages.note: The engine masks quoted spans, finds the word-and-number label, and excludes versions, counts and measures.

messages.label: is_placed("fix 5")
messages.note: The paragraph names no repository, carries no bracketed description, and links nothing, so the candidate is unplaced.

messages.label: Finding { rule: unplaceable-reference, evidence: Deterministic }
messages.note: A number candidate carries deterministic evidence, so the statistical short-circuit does not apply.

messages.label: (Error, Rewrite) in commit context, (Error, Clarify) in a transcript
messages.note: The matrix resolves the finding per context; only an error level can reach the refusal.

messages.label: exit 2, reply refused
messages.note: The hook exits 2 so the agent must revise the reply before it is sent.

flows.title: A guessed name that only advises
flows.summary: The same path for a name the engine only guesses at: the finding carries statistical evidence, the resolve matrix short-circuits it to Warning/Advise in every context, and the reply is never refused.

messages.label: "DuckDB runs fast."
messages.note: A capitalised run with an inner capital is weak evidence that it names something specific.

messages.label: Finding { evidence: Statistical }
messages.note: The name finding is tagged Statistical because the evidence is a guess, not a fact.

messages.label: (Warning, Advise) in every context
messages.note: The matrix returns before the class-and-group table is consulted, so no context, class, group or exception can turn a guess into a block.

messages.label: exit 0, reply allowed
messages.note: A warning never reaches the refusal, so the reply goes through with advice attached.

views.title: Architecture overview
views.summary: The whole path from a text source to a verdict, with the new candidate engine and placement check in the middle and the evidence-aware resolve matrix at the end.

children.title: Inside the candidate engine
children.summary: The four candidate finders the engine runs over each paragraph, and the known-names list they consult.

children.title: From finding to verdict
children.summary: How a finding's evidence reaches the resolve matrix and whether it can reach the refusal.

views.title: A reply through the stop hook
views.summary: One assistant reply, from the stop hook through the candidate engine and placement check to the refusal.

views.title: A guessed name that only advises
views.summary: The same path for a statistically-evidenced name, ending in advice rather than a refusal.

steps.heading: Text enters
steps.body: Four surfaces hand text to the writing lint; the stop hook is the one that can refuse.

steps.heading: Candidates are found
steps.body: The new engine finds numbers, phrases, times and names, masking quoted spans first.

steps.heading: Placement is checked
steps.body: Each candidate is asked whether the paragraph itself resolves it.

steps.heading: Evidence decides the level
steps.body: Statistical evidence short-circuits to Warning/Advise before the class table is read.

steps.heading: Only errors refuse
steps.body: A guessed name can never reach the refusal; a bare fix number still can.

steps.heading: The whole reply
steps.body: Watch one reply travel the full path to a refusal.

steps.heading: The guess that only advises
steps.body: The same path for a weak-evidence name ends in advice, not a block.
